title: TF Syntax Basics - Part One - Preparing the Data

cues.en: (gentle music)
cues.zh: （輕柔音樂）

cues.en: Instructor: Welcome back, everyone.
cues.zh: 歡迎大家回來。

cues.en: In this lecture, we're going to begin learning about the very syntax basics for the Keras API for TensorFlow.
cues.zh: 本堂開始學 TensorFlow Keras API 語法基礎。

cues.en: Let's head over to a notebook and get started.
cues.zh: 到筆記本開始。

cues.en: Okay, here I am at the notebook.
cues.zh: 好，現在在筆記本。

cues.en: I'm going to begin with a couple of imports.
cues.zh: 先幾個匯入。

cues.en: We'll import pandas as pd.
cues.zh: pandas as pd。

cues.en: We'll also import numpy as np.
cues.zh: numpy as np。

cues.en: And since we're gonna be doing just a little bit of visualization, I will import seaborn as sns.
cues.zh: 做一點視覺化，也 seaborn as sns。

cues.en: Now, to actually focus on the syntax of Keras, for this particular lecture, we're going to be using a very simple and actually fake dataset,
cues.zh: 為專注語法，本堂用非常簡單的假資料，

cues.en: and in the next lecture we'll be using a realistic dataset and we'll focus a lot more on feature engineering.
cues.zh: 下一堂用真實資料，更專注特徵工程。

cues.en: Let's go ahead and read in this file.
cues.zh: 讀檔。

cues.en: We'll use pd.read_csv and then underneath our data folder, there's a file called fake_reg, for regression, .csv.
cues.zh: pd.read_csv，data 資料夾下 fake_reg.csv，reg 代表 regression。

cues.en: And then, we'll check out the head of this dataframe.
cues.zh: 看 head。

cues.en: So this dataframe, it's very, very simple.
cues.zh: 很簡單。

cues.en: It simply has a price, and then two corresponding features.
cues.zh: 只有 price 與兩個對應特徵。

cues.en: So we're gonna treat this as a regression problem where based off feature1 and feature2, we'll attempt to predict the price.
cues.zh: 當迴歸問題，依 feature1、feature2 預測價格。

cues.en: So we can imagine that maybe these are measurements of some rare gemstones where the gemstone has feature1 and then feature2, and we're trying to predict the price.
cues.zh: 可想像稀有寶石的測量，有兩特徵，要預測價格。

cues.en: So here we have historical information, which means this is a supervised learning problem.
cues.zh: 有歷史資訊，所以監督式。

cues.en: Our main goal is to build a model that when we pick a new gemstone from the ground, we can measure its features, feature1 and feature2, and predict what price we should be selling this
cues.zh: 目標是挖到新寶石時，量兩特徵，預測市場

cues.en: at the market due to the fact that we have historical information on the price sold based off these two features.
cues.zh: 售價，因為有過去兩特徵對售價資訊。

cues.en: So a very simple dataset.
cues.zh: 很簡單。

cues.en: I wanna quickly show you how we could explore this dataset.
cues.zh: 快速展示如何探索。

cues.en: We'll say create a pair plot of the dataframe, run that, and then we'll be able to see the features versus the price.
cues.zh: 對 DataFrame 建 pairplot，執行，看到特徵對價格。

cues.en: And you'll notice that, especially feature2, it seems to have very high correlation with the actual price; so this kinda is another indicator that this is fake data.
cues.zh: 尤其 feature2，與價格高度相關，也暗示是假資料。

cues.en: So in a realistic data set, which we're gonna do in the very next lecture, we would take a lot of time exploring this data doing what's known as exploratory data analysis,
cues.zh: 下一堂真實資料時，會花很多時間探索，

cues.en: performing a lot of visualizations, as well as possibly performing some feature engineering trying to extract other features from features that we can't quite use.
cues.zh: 視覺化，也可能從不能直接用的特徵，抽新特徵。

cues.en: However, let's focus really on the main workflow for using Keras and TensorFlow for deep learning.
cues.zh: 但先專注 Keras、TensorFlow 深度學習工作流。

cues.en: So step number one is to read in your data.
cues.zh: 第一步讀資料。

cues.en: And then once you've done feature engineering your data, once you've explored your data, the next step is to create a test_train_split.
cues.zh: 探索、特徵工程後，下一步 train_test_split。

cues.en: And we can do this from scikit-learns, model selection,
cues.zh: scikit-learn 的 model_selection

cues.en: has a train_test_split functionality which is really easy to use.
cues.zh: 有很容易用的 train_test_split。

cues.en: So what we're gonna do is we're gonna use this train_test_split function to split our data into a training set and a test set.
cues.zh: 我們要使用 train_test_split 函數，把資料分成訓練集與測試集。

cues.en: So we'll train on the training set and then evaluate our model's performance on the test set.
cues.zh: 在訓練集上訓練模型，再用測試集評估模型的表現。

cues.en: So first what we wanna do is we want to grab the features that we're going to use.
cues.zh: 先取要用的特徵。

cues.en: So in this case, that will be feature1 and feature2.
cues.zh: 這裡 feature1、feature2。

cues.en: And because of the way TensorFlow works, we have to actually pass in NumPy arrays instead of Pandas dataframes or Pandas series.
cues.zh: 依 TensorFlow 運作，要傳 NumPy 陣列，不是 pandas DataFrame 或 Series。

cues.en: So I can simply add .values to the end of a series or dataframe and it'll return it back as a NumPy array.
cues.zh: 尾端加 .values 就回 NumPy 陣列。

cues.en: So what we're gonna do is we're gonna grab features and set that as X.
cues.zh: 取特徵設 X。

cues.en: And by convention, we use capital X because typically the feature matrix is two-dimensional, so we indicate that with a capital.
cues.zh: 慣例大寫 X，因為通常特徵矩陣二維。

cues.en: And then, the label that we're going to predict, our y, is the price column.
cues.zh: 要預測的 y，是 price 欄。

cues.en: And same thing here, we'll grab values.
cues.zh: 也取 values。

cues.en: And again, by convention, since the price is essentially a one-dimensional vector, we have lowercase y for that.
cues.zh: 價格基本上一維向量，所以 y 小寫。

cues.en: So that's why we have uppercase X and lowercase y: it essentially stems from the way you would write this down mathematically on paper.
cues.zh: 大 X、小 y 源自紙上數學記法。

cues.en: So now that we have our actual NumPy arrays, so if we take a look at X, it's just a NumPy array of the same information we had in that dataframe for feature1 and feature2, it's just NumPy instead of Pandas,
cues.zh: 看 X，是同樣兩特徵的 NumPy 陣列，資料相同，只是不用 pandas。

cues.en: it's time for our train_test_split.
cues.zh: 該分割。

cues.en: So the way I like to do this is simply call train_test_split, and after you've imported it, you should be able to do Shift + Tab to see the documentation string.
cues.zh: 匯入 train_test_split 後，按 Shift + Tab 看文件。

cues.en: Expand on it, go ahead and scroll down, and eventually at the bottom you'll see something called Examples, and to save myself a little bit of time, I like to just
cues.zh: 展開、往下，到 Examples，省時間，喜歡

cues.en: copy and paste this line from the example, which is essentially showing you how you would actually use this.
cues.zh: 複製範例那行，展示實際用法。

cues.en: So I'm going to paste that in and then put this all in one line and essentially explain what's going on here.
cues.zh: 貼上、整理一行，解釋。

cues.en: Recall that when we do a train_test_split, we both split our features into X_train and X_test as well as our labels into y_train and y_test.
cues.zh: 分割 X 成 X_train/X_test，也分 y 成 y_train/y_test。

cues.en: Make sure you review the machine learning section of the course in case you have any questions on what these four parameters or variables actually represent.
cues.zh: 不清楚四變數，複習機器學習部分。

cues.en: Then, for train_test_split, you pass in all your features as X, your labels as y, and then you choose a percentage as your test size.
cues.zh: 傳全部特徵 X、標籤 y，再選測試比例。

cues.en: So typically, you use maybe around 30% of your data.
cues.zh: 通常約 30%。

cues.en: So if I said 0.3, that's going to be 30% of my total data will be used for the test set.
cues.zh: 0.3 就總資料 30% 作測試。

cues.en: And you can always make this smaller if you have really large data sets.
cues.zh: 大資料可更小。

cues.en: And then there's the random_state.
cues.zh: 再 random_state。

cues.en: So the train_test_split is going to perform this split randomly; so it's gonna grab random rows and then split them into the training side and the test side.
cues.zh: 分割隨機取列，分到訓練與測試。

cues.en: If you want to repeat the actual results of the split the same every time, then you would set a random state to a specific number.
cues.zh: 想每次一樣，random_state 設特定數。

cues.en: The number itself is just an arbitrary choice; you just have to make sure to choose the same one each time.
cues.zh: 數字任意，確保每次同一個即可。

cues.en: So go ahead and choose random_state=42 and that way you will get the same random split that I do.
cues.zh: 選 random_state=42，和我相同。

cues.en: So we'll go ahead and run this.
cues.zh: 執行。

cues.en: And now, we've split up our data and we can actually check this by checking the shape of this.
cues.zh: 分好，可用 shape 確認。

cues.en: So notice X_train.shape is now 700 by 2 features and X_test.shape
cues.zh: X_train.shape 是 700 乘 2 特徵，X_test.shape

cues.en: is 300 by 2 features.
So here's 70% of our data as a training set and 30% as a test set since our total size of the original data was 1000 rows.
cues.zh: 原本一千列，70% 訓練、30% 測試。

cues.en: Okay, now typically the next step is to actually normalize or scale your data.
cues.zh: 通常下一步正規化或縮放。

cues.en: Because we're working with weights and biases inside of a neural network, if we have really large values in our feature set that could cause errors with the weights.
cues.zh: 網路有權重偏差，特徵值太大可能影響權重、造成錯誤。

cues.en: And later on, we'll talk about vanishing and exploding gradients; that could be an issue.
cues.zh: 稍後梯度消失、爆炸會談。

cues.en: But one way to try to avoid any issues when training your network is to normalize and scale your feature data.
cues.zh: 訓練避免問題的一種方法，是縮放、正規化特徵。

cues.en: So scikit-learn actually allows us to do this quite simply by saying from sklearn.preprocessing import.
cues.zh: scikit-learn 很簡單，from sklearn.preprocessing import。

cues.en: And there's actually lots of different ways you can normalize or scale your data.
cues.zh: 有很多縮放方法。

cues.en: One simple way is to use what's known as MinMax scaling.
cues.zh: 一種簡單是 MinMax。

cues.en: So we'll go ahead and import MinMaxScaler, and if you call help on MinMaxScaler, it will actually describe what this is doing.
cues.zh: 匯入 MinMaxScaler，help 會解釋。

cues.en: So essentially, it's going to transform your data based off the standard deviation of your data as well as the min and the max values.
cues.zh: 基本上依資料標準差，以及最小最大值轉換。

cues.en: So you can see here the actual formulation that it's running for us.
cues.zh: 這裡實際公式。

cues.en: So what we're gonna do is show you how you can scale your data, which is very typical in your workflow for dealing with neural networks.
cues.zh: 示範縮放，是神經網路工作流常見步驟。

cues.en: Now you don't have to actually scale the label, and if you take a look at our provided notebook, we have a link explaining why we don't need to scale the label.
cues.zh: 不必縮放標籤，講義有原因連結。

cues.en: We really only need to scale the features since that's essentially what's being passed through the actual network.
cues.zh: 只需縮放特徵，因為實際經過網路。

cues.en: The final label is just a comparison done at the end.
cues.zh: 最後標籤只在尾端比較。

cues.en: So to use a scaler with scikit-learn, what we do is we first create an instance of it.
cues.zh: 用 scaler，先建實例。

cues.en: So we choose some variable name, typically scaler, and then we create an instance of our MinMaxScaler, open close parentheses.
cues.zh: 選變數名，通常 scaler，再 MinMaxScaler()。

cues.en: So now, I have this instance of this scaler and what I'm going to do is I need to actually fit the scaler onto my training data.
cues.zh: 有實例後，擬合訓練資料。

cues.en: So I'll say fit on X_train.
cues.zh: fit(X_train)。

cues.en: And what fit does is it simply calculates the parameters it needs to perform the actual scaling later on.
cues.zh: fit 只算稍後縮放所需參數。

cues.en: So if we recall from calling help on MinMaxScaler, the MinMaxScaler is dependent on the standard deviation, the minimum value, and the maximum value
cues.zh: 回想 help，MinMaxScaler 依標準差、最小、最大值，

cues.en: within that particular dataset.
cues.zh: 在該資料集中，

cues.en: So what fit does is it essentially calculates the standard deviation, the min and max; so that's what fit does.
cues.zh: fit 基本上計算標準差、min、max。

cues.en: So we run fit on our training set and the reason we only run it on the training set is because we want to prevent what's known as data leakage from the test set.
cues.zh: 只在訓練集 fit，是防止測試集資料洩漏。

cues.en: We don't want to assume that we have prior information of the test set, so we only fit our scaler to the training set to not try to cheat and look into the test set.
cues.zh: 不假設事先知道測試資訊，所以只 fit 訓練，避免偷看測試作弊。

cues.en: Then what we need to do is transform our training data: so we'll say X_train is now equal
cues.zh: 再轉換訓練，X_train 等於

cues.en: to scaler.transform on X_train.
cues.zh: scaler.transform(X_train)。

cues.en: That actually performs a transformation.
cues.zh: 實際做轉換。

cues.en: So there's essentially two steps here: we fit, which is calculate what's needed for the transformation to occur, and then we actually perform the transformation.
cues.zh: 兩步，fit 計算轉換所需，transform 實際執行。

cues.en: And we'll do the same for the test set; so we'll say scaler.transform on X_test.
cues.zh: 測試也 scaler.transform(X_test)。

cues.en: And now, if we take a look at these values for X_train, you'll notice they have been scaled.
cues.zh: 看 X_train，已縮放。

cues.en: So if we take a look at what the max value on X_train is, it's now 1, and then the minimum value is now 0.
cues.zh: 最大現在 1，最小 0。

cues.en: So everything's been scaled to now be between 0 and 1.
cues.zh: 全部在 0 到 1。

cues.en: And again, we're only fitting on the training set to not ascertain information from the test set because that's essentially cheating.
cues.zh: 再次，只擬合訓練，不取得測試資訊，否則作弊。

cues.en: Okay, so now that we've scaled the data, it's time to actually show you how to create your neural network; so in part two of this lecture,
cues.zh: 好，縮放後，展示建網路。第二部分，

cues.en: we'll begin creating our neural network.
cues.zh: 開始建立。

cues.en: I'll see you there.
cues.zh: 到時見。
